chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Salamat ibn al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Daylami, the servant of Al-Rida, who said: I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever sends three believers on the Hajj pilgrimage has indeed bought himself from God, the Mighty and Majestic, with that price, and He will not ask him from where he earned his wealth, whether it is from halal or haram.
ai.seo_question: Does God question the source of wealth when someone pays for three people to perform Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith in *Al-Kisāl* to emphasize the spiritual efficacy of facilitating collective worship, noting that the Imam accepts the financial transaction as a valid purchase of salvation without scrutinizing the purity of the wealth's source. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the act of enabling others to perform obligatory duties carries immense reward, prioritizing the facilitation of the ritual over the strict audit of the donor's capital. It underscores the generosity of God in accepting the 'price' of salvation based on the sincerity of the act rather than the meticulous origin of the funds.
